1.title: Getting Started

2.text: pnpm 10+ on Node 22+, or mise — if pnpm isn't installed, the CLI installs mise and uses it to fetch node + pnpm An AI coding agent that supports Agent Skills — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose, … Setup asks which ones to install the skills for. Obsidian — optional but recommended
2.title: Requirements

3.text:
npx claude-second-brain Or install globally for a shorter command (csb is an alias): npm i -g claude-second-brain
csb                    # same as: claude-second-brain The CLI will ask: Brain name — what to call this brain (default: my-brain) Git remote — optionally host your vault on GitHub (requires gh CLI) or Cloudflare Artifacts (requires a Cloudflare account + wrangler) Register qmd collections after install? — runs pnpm qmd:setup once dependencies are installed Install skills for which agents? — Claude Code plus any detected agent is preselected; see Install skills for any agent Every question is asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended. Creates the brain at ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/, registers it in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml, runs pnpm install (using your system pnpm 10+, or mise to fetch node + pnpm if it's missing), registers the qmd collections, installs the skills for the agents you picked, and runs git init.
3.title: Step 1 — Scaffold

4.text: cd ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain && pnpm qmd:reindex Generates local vector embeddings. First run downloads ~2GB of GGUF models — once.
4.title: Step 2 — Generate vector embeddings

5.text:
If you created a GitHub repo during setup, it's already pushed — skip straight to opening in Obsidian. If you skipped GitHub during setup, connect it now: git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main Open ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/ as a vault in Obsidian — the folder is already a valid Obsidian vault. The Git plugin is pre-configured — enable it and sync is automatic.
5.title: Step 3 — Open in Obsidian (and push to GitHub if not done)

6.text: Run npx claude-second-brain (or csb if installed globally) again to create additional brains. Each gets its own folder under ~/.claude-second-brain/ and its own isolated qmd index. The global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh) always operate on the default brain in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. The first brain created is set as the default automatically. See the CLI Reference for ls, use, rm, path, qmd, exec, skills, git-token, and doctor subcommands that manage and target specific brains.
6.title: Multiple brains

7.text: Edit anywhere — your agent on desktop, web or mobile. The vault is a plain git repo, so any agent that can clone it can work on it: run it locally, or use a cloud agent with GitHub access (Claude Code on the web and mobile, Codex cloud, Copilot coding agent, Cursor background agents, …) to ingest a source, run a query, or update a page from your phone. Read anywhere — Obsidian desktop and mobile. Open the repo as an Obsidian vault. The bundled .obsidian folder pre-configures obsidian-git — no setup required. Your wiki syncs automatically on every commit. For iPhone and iPad, see iCloud sync. Browse anywhere — your git host. It's a plain git repo. On GitHub (or any host with a web UI), view and edit files directly in the browser at any time.
7.title: Access from anywhere

8.text: The claude-second-brain CLI creates and manages brains registered in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml.
8.title: Commands

9.text: Run it without installing anything: npx claude-second-brain pnpm dlx claude-second-brain bunx claude-second-brain
9.title: Usage

10.text:
Install it globally to get the shorter csb alias. Every page in this reference uses csb; substitute npx claude-second-brain if you haven't installed it. npm install -g claude-second-brain
csb ls pnpm add -g claude-second-brain
csb ls bun add -g claude-second-brain
csb ls
10.title: Global install

11.text: csb [<name>]: Create a new brain. Interactive unless you pass a name and flags. csb ls: List all registered brains. The default brain is marked with *. csb use <name>: Set the default brain. csb rm [<name>…]: Delete one or more brains, and optionally their remotes. csb path [qmd|config|root]: Print a path for the default (or named) brain. csb qmd <qmd args…>: Run qmd against the default (or named) brain. csb exec -- <cmd…>: Run a command inside the default (or named) brain's directory. csb skills: Install or update the wiki skills for any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …). csb git-token [<name>]: Renew the git push/pull token for a Cloudflare Artifacts brain. csb doctor: Verify your setup and suggest fixes. ls is also available as list, rm as remove, and use as default or switch.
11.title: Available commands

12.text:
Show usage. Works on its own, after any command, or as csb help <command>. csb --help
csb rm --help
csb help qmd
12.title: -h, --help

13.text: Variable Description CSB_AGENTS Agents to install skills for, comma-separated or all. Used by csb and csb skills when --agent is not passed. CSB_USE_MISE Set to 1 to always fetch node and pnpm with mise, even if pnpm 10+ is on your PATH. CSB_ICONS nerd, emoji or none: icons in the git-remote picker. Nerd Font logos are on by default in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty. CSB_SKIP_SKILL_UPDATES Set to 1 to update outdated global skills without prompting. CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN API token with Artifacts Read and Edit. Used instead of your wrangler login. CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID Cloudflare account to use when your login can see more than one. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Where Claude Code reads its config. Skills for Claude Code go in its skills/ folder.
13.title: Environment variables

14.text: Every command exits non-zero on failure (an unknown brain name, a missing config, a failed doctor check, a remote that could not be created) and writes the error to stderr.
14.title: Exit status

15.text: The wiki ships with a set of Agent Skills that cover the full workflow, and they work in any agent that supports skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. No manual prompting, no copy-pasting.
15.title: Skills

16.text: /brain-ingest — Drop a file into raw-sources/. Your agent summarizes the source, creates a wiki/sources/ page, updates related topic pages, and flags contradictions. /brain-search — Ask anything. Your agent runs hybrid search, reads the most relevant pages, and writes an answer with inline [[wiki/page]] citations. /lint — Health-check the wiki. Surfaces orphan pages, broken links, unresolved contradictions, and data gaps.
16.title: Daily workflow

17.text: /brain-refresh — Re-scan the vault and regenerate vector embeddings for new or changed files. /brain-rebuild — Destructive. Redesigns the qmd schema, drops the old index, and rebuilds from scratch. Use only when the current structure no longer fits how you search.
17.title: Maintenance

18.text:
The skills follow the Agent Skills format, so they work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. /brain-ingest, /brain-search, and /brain-refresh install globally during setup — once to ~/.agents/skills/, with symlinks from agent-specific folders like ~/.claude/skills/. /brain-rebuild and /lint live inside the vault at .claude/skills/ and are copied to .agents/skills/ and other agents' folders for the agents you pick. To install for more agents later, or after upgrading the CLI: npx claude-second-brain skills --agent codex,cursor,github-copilot See Install skills for any agent for the full layout. To pull in improvements from the latest template: # Install or update all 5 wiki skills
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills -a claude-code -y

# Or update a specific skill
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills --skill brain-ingest -a claude-code -y Once installed via npx skills, future updates are a single command: npx skills update -a claude-code
18.title: Install or update skills

19.text: This is not a RAG system. It's not a chatbot over your notes. It's an actively maintained, cross-linked wiki — five structured page types, YAML frontmatter, and a set of agent skills — usable from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, or any agent that supports Agent Skills — that run the whole thing. The schema (CLAUDE.md) is that idea file. Your agent reads it every session (other agents reach it through AGENTS.md).
19.title: How this is different

20.text: Tool Role Your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …) Reads sources, writes wiki pages, cross-links, flags contradictions qmd Local hybrid search (vector + BM25) across your entire wiki Obsidian Graph view, backlinks, mobile reading — offline, no extra sync Git (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, …) Source of truth — version history, your agent anywhere, Obsidian sync Everything is pre-configured. You bring the sources. Next: Get started in 3 steps →
20.title: The stack

21.text: A running record of every released version of claude-second-brain on npm. Newest releases first. For auto-generated notes and tags, see the GitHub releases page.

22.text: Bug fixes for CLI argument handling, plus a test suite. Fixes: Brain names are validated before scaffolding. Names that are empty, . / .., or contain path separators, quotes or control characters are rejected, so a name can no longer escape ~/.claude-second-brain/ or corrupt config.toml. --brain now requires a value in path, qmd, exec, skills and git-token. Previously a bare --brain silently fell back to the default brain (so csb git-token --brain renewed the wrong brain's token). csb exec … -- <cmd> --help and csb qmd … -- … --help now pass --help through to the command after -- instead of printing csb's own help. Tests and CI: New pnpm test (node --test tests/*.test.js) covering brain-name validation, --brain parsing and help pass-through; a Test workflow runs it on pull requests and main. Docs: README and docs home link /brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh, /brain-rebuild and /lint to their docs pages.

Added npm keywords matching the GitHub repo topics (ai, amp, claude-code, codex, cursor, github, knowledge-base, knowledge-graph, knowledge-management, llm, obsidian, obsidian-vault, qmd, second-brain) so the package is searchable on npmjs.com. npm homepage now points to the docs site instead of the GitHub README, and bugs links to GitHub issues.

24.text: Maintenance release: security updates and a tokenless release pipeline. No CLI or template changes. Security: Refreshed dependencies to clear all Dependabot alerts (pnpm audit: 106 → 0). @clack/prompts is now ^1.9.0; transitive docs-site deps (hono, vite, mermaid, dompurify, …) resolve to patched versions, with pnpm overrides for toml, katex and @hono/node-server. Removed the stale package-lock.json; the repo uses pnpm only. Release pipeline: npm releases use trusted publishing (OIDC) from release-publish.yml with --provenance, so no NPM_TOKEN is stored in the repo. npm comes from mise.toml (11.21.2; trusted publishing needs 11.5.1+). v1.2.0 was the first release published this way. CI: Docs workflows install Playwright browsers from the locked version (1.65.1).
24.title: v1.2.1 — 2026-11-27

25.text: Works with any agent, not just Claude Code, plus a faster, unattended setup and first-class Cloudflare Artifacts git tokens. Existing installs: run csb skills once to move global skills from ~/.claude/skills to ~/.agents/skills (the old copies become symlinks). Agents: Skills install for any Agent Skills agent, with the same layout as npx skills: global skills are written once to ~/.agents/skills/<name> and symlinked into agent-specific dirs (~/.claude/skills, ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills, ~/.config/goose/skills, …). Supported: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Amp, Cline, Windsurf, Goose, Kiro CLI, Roo Code, Continue, Junie, Augment. Vault-local skills (brain-rebuild, lint) are copied into each selected agent's project skills dir (.agents/skills/, .windsurf/skills/, …). New --agent, -a <ids> (comma-separated or all) and CSB_AGENTS to pick agents; --copy to copy instead of symlink. Interactive setup preselects Claude Code plus every detected agent. New csb skills [--agent <ids>] [--copy] [--brain <name>] to add agents or update skills later, and csb skills --list to show supported agents and their skills dirs. New vaults ship an AGENTS.md that points Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other agents at CLAUDE.md. The Next steps box shows how to open each agent you picked (claude, codex, cursor ., …). Setup: All prompts, including the qmd-registration question, are asked up front; the rest runs unattended. Long steps show a live spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line. If pnpm 10+ is on your PATH, it's used directly; otherwise the CLI installs mise and fetches node + pnpm. CSB_USE_MISE=1 forces mise. The git-remote picker shows GitHub / Cloudflare logos as Nerd Font glyphs in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty, emoji elsewhere. Override with CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none. If the remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, the problem and fix are listed in Next steps, and the CLI exits 1. Cloudflare Artifacts: Switched to the account-scoped REST API (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…); the old artifacts.cloudflare.net/v1/api host is no longer used. Set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID when your login can see more than one account. A deleted or inactive namespace is recreated automatically before the repo is created. Setup now saves a 90-day git token in the vault's .git/config (http.<remote>.extraHeader), so git push / git pull and obsidian-git just work. No more 24-hour token to copy. New csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print] renews it (default 90 days, max 1 year), replacing the manual curl renewal. Other: csb doctor accepts system pnpm 10+ in place of mise and checks that the global skills in ~/.agents/skills match the installed release. README, docs and package description say "any agent" and "git" (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, or any remote) instead of Claude Code and GitHub only. "Claude reads it" and similar wording is now agent-neutral, and "Access from anywhere" covers any local or cloud agent and any git host.

26.text: CLI UX pass. Every addition is non-breaking — the -- in csb qmd -- … and the path --qmd / --config / --root flag form continue to work, with a stderr deprecation notice on the flag form. CLI: Added csb use <name> (aliases default, switch) to set the default brain without editing ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Runs the same header-rewrite path as csb rm. Added csb exec [--brain <name>] -- <cmd…> — runs any command inside the resolved brain's directory with INDEX_PATH pre-set. csb qmd now delegates to the same helper. Added csb doctor — checks for gh (+ auth), mise, wrangler, the central config, each brain's path and qmd_index, and whether the default brain resolves. Prints a Fix: hint under each failed check. csb path now accepts positional subcommands: csb path [qmd|config|root]. The --qmd / --config / --root flag form still works with a stderr deprecation warning. Every subcommand routes --help / -h to its own topic help. csb help <command> also prints per-command help. Top-level help shows the config path and current default brain. csb rm gained --delete-remote and --keep-remote for scripting. Under -y with neither flag, remotes are preserved (safe default). resolveBrain() error now points to csb use <name> as the fix.
26.title: v1.1.0 — 2026-04-19

27.text: First major release. Brains now live at ~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/ (not the repo root), and global skills resolve paths at call time via new CLI subcommands instead of baked-in paths. Existing single-brain installs: re-run npx claude-second-brain <name> to migrate. Legacy active = … in config.toml is auto-rewritten to default = …. CLI: Added claude-second-brain path [--brain N] [--root|--qmd|--config] and claude-second-brain qmd [--brain N] -- … subcommands. The global skills now resolve paths at call time via these commands instead of having absolute paths baked in at scaffold time. Added claude-second-brain rm [<name>…] with multi-select (space to toggle) and a follow-up prompt to delete the git remote. config.toml's active field renamed to default. Existing configs with active = … are still read transparently and rewritten to default = … on the next write. Global skills (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh) now ship with a .csb-version sidecar file. Re-running npx claude-second-brain <name> detects version mismatches and prompts before overwriting; CSB_SKIP_SKILL_UPDATES=1 disables the prompt. npx claude-second-brain now auto-registers qmd collections during scaffold — no manual /setup step needed afterwards. Added csb as a bin alias. After npm i -g claude-second-brain, both claude-second-brain and csb are available globally. Skills: Removed /setup and /qmd-cli — their responsibilities are absorbed by create.js (auto-registration) and /brain-refresh / the csb qmd proxy respectively. Added /update-workflows to audit pack-test.yml drift against current repo state. Split /release into /package-release (version bump + PR) and an orchestrator /release that additionally runs /update-workflows and /update-docs. Refactors: Removed the __QMD_PATH__ and __CSB_CONFIG__ placeholder substitutions. scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts now compute the index path from import.meta.url; CLAUDE.md and vault-local skills use a relative .qmd/index.sqlite path. patchVault() now only substitutes __BRAIN_NAME__ in template/README.md. Global skills ship unmodified from the template. Fixes: writeConfig() now writes default = … when upserting into a pre-existing empty or default-less config.toml. Previously a zero-byte config.toml blocked the field from being written and left CLI subcommands unable to resolve a default brain. pnpm qmd:setup failures during scaffolding now surface captured stderr (last ~10 lines) instead of a generic "failed" message. template/scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts wrap their bodies in try/catch that prints a tagged error with vault + db paths and exits 1, replacing silent unhandled rejections. resolveBrain() errors now list available brain names and include a fix hint. Docs: Getting-started, per-skill docs, and vocs sidebar updated to reflect the 5-skill surface (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh, brain-rebuild, lint). Documented rm multi-select and remote-deletion prompts. /setup skill reference removed from quick-start in favor of pnpm qmd:reindex.

39.text: Destructive. Redesign the qmd schema from scratch. Use only when the current collection/context structure no longer fits how you search — for example, when the wiki has grown into new domains that deserve their own collections. What it does: Analyzes the current wiki. Proposes new collections and contexts. Waits for your approval before any destructive action. Patches scripts/qmd/setup.ts, drops the old index, and rebuilds embeddings from scratch. Scope: vault-local, installed at .claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. .agents/skills/brain-rebuild). Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md.
39.title: /brain-rebuild

40.text: Ingest a new source into the wiki. Drop a file into raw-sources/articles/, raw-sources/pdfs/, or raw-sources/personal/, then run /brain-ingest. Your agent will: Read the source in full. Summarize it in 3–5 bullets and ask you what matters most. Create a wiki/sources/[slug].md page with abstract, key claims, notable quotes, and your synthesis note. Update or create topic/entity pages that the source touches, integrating it as prose (not copy-paste) with source attribution. Flag contradictions with [!WARNING] callouts on any page where the new source disagrees with existing claims. Log the ingest in wiki/log.md. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-ingest). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md.
40.title: /brain-ingest

41.text: Query the wiki to answer a question. Runs hybrid search (vector + BM25) across the entire wiki, reads the 2–5 most relevant pages, and synthesizes an answer with inline [[wiki/page]] citations. Flags gaps where the wiki has no coverage. If the answer pulls together multiple pages in a novel way, it offers to file it as a permanent wiki/qa/[slug].md entry — so the synthesis compounds next time. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-search). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md.
41.title: /brain-search

42.text: Refresh the qmd index. Re-scans all collections for new or changed files and regenerates vector embeddings. Run after a bulk ingest session or manual edits to the wiki. Pass force to re-embed every chunk — useful after changing the embedding model. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-refresh). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md.
42.title: /brain-refresh

43.text: Health-check the wiki. Reports on: Orphan pages — wiki pages with no inbound [[links]]. Unresolved contradictions — pages with [!WARNING] Contradiction callouts that haven't been resolved. Stale claims — claims superseded by newer sources. Missing pages — concepts/entities referenced by [[links]] that lack their own page. Broken links — wikilinks pointing to files that don't exist. Data gaps — important topics that lack source coverage; suggests specific sources to investigate. Applies fixes where safe and flags everything else for your review. Appends a summary to wiki/log.md. Scope: vault-local, installed at .claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. .agents/skills/lint). Source: template/.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md.
43.title: /lint

44.text: Cloudflare Artifacts is a git-compatible object storage remote. It's a good choice if you don't want to use GitHub — your vault data stays on Cloudflare's infrastructure and never touches GitHub.
44.title: Cloudflare Artifacts remote

45.text: A Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (required for Artifacts) Either wrangler login (the CLI runs it for you and requests artifacts:write), or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN set to an API token with Artifacts › Read and Artifacts › Edit If your login can see more than one account, set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID (or pick it when prompted) wrangler CLI — if not installed, the setup wizard falls back to npx wrangler automatically
45.title: Prerequisites

46.text: When you run npx claude-second-brain and select Cloudflare Artifacts as your remote, the CLI handles everything: Checks wrangler auth (logs you in and requests the artifacts:write scope if needed) Resolves your account ID and creates a new Artifacts repo via the Artifacts REST API (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…) Runs git remote add origin <remote-url> Pushes the initial commit Mints a 90-day git token and saves it in the vault's .git/config, so git push / git pull just work
46.title: Setup (automatic)

47.text:
If you skipped Cloudflare Artifacts during setup, or setup failed, you can connect an existing brain by hand. These are the same REST API calls the CLI makes: # 1. Credentials: a wrangler login token (or your own CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and your account ID
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN:-$(npx wrangler auth token)}"
export CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=<your-account-id>   # shown by `npx wrangler whoami`
API=https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/artifacts

# 2. Create the namespace (skip if it already exists)
curl -s -X POST "$API/namespaces" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"namespace":"default"}'

# 3. Create the repo. The response's result.remote is the git URL and result.token a 24-hour push token
curl -s -X POST "$API/namespaces/default/repos" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"my-brain","default_branch":"main"}'

# 4. From the vault root: add the remote and push with that token
git remote add origin <result.remote>   # https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.artifacts.cloudflare.net/git/default/my-brain.git
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer <result.token>" push -u origin main

# 5. Save a 90-day token so plain git push / git pull (and obsidian-git) work
csb git-token my-brain To remove the repo later: curl -X DELETE "$API/namespaces/default/repos/my-brain" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN".
47.title: Manual setup

48.text:
Artifacts git tokens expire (csb mints them for 90 days; Cloudflare allows up to 1 year). When git push or git pull starts failing with an auth error, renew it: csb git-token            # default brain
csb git-token my-brain   # a specific brain This mints a new repo-scoped token with your wrangler login (or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and stores it for the brain's remote as http.<remote>.extraHeader in the vault's .git/config — local only, never committed. Plain git push / git pull (and obsidian-git) work again until it expires. Options: --ttl <duration> for a different lifetime (seconds, or 12h, 90d, 1y; max 1 year), --read for a read-only token, --print to print the token instead of saving it (e.g. for another machine: git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer $(csb git-token --print)" pull).
48.title: Renewing the git token

49.text: During setup, the CLI asks for an Artifacts namespace (default: default). Namespaces scope repos within your Cloudflare account — useful if you manage multiple projects. For personal use, the default is fine.
49.title: Namespace

50.text: If the repo can't be created or the first push fails, the CLI still creates the brain locally but says so in a warning, lists the fix in Next steps, and exits non-zero. A 403 / Authentication error usually means Artifacts isn't enabled on the account (Workers Paid plan), the token is missing the Artifacts permission, or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID points at another account. A 404 / Namespace is not active means the namespace was deleted; the CLI recreates it and retries automatically, and if that still fails, wait a minute (deletion can take a moment to finish) or pick another namespace. Fix it, then csb rm <name> and re-run, or add any other git remote by hand.
50.title: If setup fails

51.text: GitHub is the default Git backend for claude-second-brain. Your vault is stored as a private GitHub repository — you get version history, access from any device, and Obsidian mobile sync via the bundled Git plugin.
51.title: GitHub remote

52.text: A GitHub account gh CLI — used for authentication and repo creation during setup
52.title: Prerequisites

53.text: When you run npx claude-second-brain and select GitHub as your remote, the CLI handles everything: Checks gh auth status — runs gh auth login if not authenticated Creates a private repo: gh repo create <name> --private --source=. --remote=origin --push Pushes the initial commit
53.title: Setup (automatic)

54.text:
If you skipped GitHub during setup, or gh wasn't installed, connect it manually: # With gh CLI
gh repo create my-brain --private --source=. --remote=origin --push

# Without gh CLI
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main
54.title: Manual setup

55.text: The vault ships with obsidian-git enabled, so Obsidian commits, pulls and pushes on a schedule. For iPhone and iPad, see iCloud sync.
55.title: Syncing from Obsidian

56.text: Obsidian on iPhone and iPad opens vaults stored in iCloud Drive → Obsidian. The reliable way to get your brain there is a second clone of its git repo in that folder, kept in sync by obsidian-git on your Mac. Your phone reads it through iCloud and never runs git.
56.title: iCloud sync

57.text: Putting the brain itself in iCloud Drive causes trouble: iCloud syncs .git file by file, and can leave conflicted copies inside it that corrupt the repo. node_modules and the qmd index (.qmd/) would be uploaded to iCloud and downloaded to your phone, which doesn't need them. obsidian-git's mobile support is described by its author as very unstable, and it can't use the rebase sync method the vault ships with. A second clone avoids all three: its .git lives outside iCloud, it has no node_modules or index, and only your Mac runs git.
57.title: Why not just move the brain into iCloud?

58.text: Your agent works in the brain as usual (~/.claude-second-brain/<name>) and pushes to the git remote. Obsidian on your Mac opens the iCloud clone. obsidian-git there pulls the agent's changes, and commits and pushes anything you edit, including edits made on your phone. iCloud copies the clone's notes to your iPhone and iPad.
58.title: How it fits together

59.text:
On your Mac, with Obsidian installed on a device signed in to the same iCloud account (that creates the iCloud~md~obsidian folder): ICLOUD=~/Library/Mobile\ Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents
BRAIN="$(csb path)"                                   # or: csb path --brain <name>
REMOTE="$(git -C "$BRAIN" remote get-url origin)"

# Clone into iCloud, but keep the .git folder outside it
git clone --separate-git-dir ~/.claude-second-brain/.icloud-git/my-brain "$REMOTE" "$ICLOUD/my-brain" For a Cloudflare Artifacts remote, the clone needs the brain's git token. Copy it from the brain's config before cloning, and save it in the clone afterwards: HEADER="$(git -C "$BRAIN" config --get "http.$REMOTE.extraHeader")"
git -c http.extraHeader="$HEADER" clone --separate-git-dir ~/.claude-second-brain/.icloud-git/my-brain "$REMOTE" "$ICLOUD/my-brain"
git -C "$ICLOUD/my-brain" config "http.$REMOTE.extraHeader" "$HEADER" When the token expires, run csb git-token and copy the header again. Then: In Obsidian on your Mac, Open folder as vault and pick the clone in iCloud Drive → Obsidian. obsidian-git is already on. On your iPhone or iPad, open Obsidian and choose the vault from the iCloud list. On the phone, open Settings → Git, and under Advanced turn on Disable on this device. That setting is stored per device, so the Mac keeps syncing.
59.title: Set it up

60.text: Edits on your phone reach git the next time your Mac is awake, iCloud has synced, and obsidian-git commits (5 minutes after the last change). In Finder, right-click the clone and choose Keep Downloaded, so "Optimize Mac Storage" doesn't offload notes. Don't turn on Obsidian Sync for this vault as well. Two sync systems on one vault fight over the same files. Not on Apple devices? Clone the repo on each device instead, or use obsidian-git's mobile support (switch its sync method to Merge, and expect rough edges).
60.title: Tips

61.text: Every vault ships with the obsidian-git community plugin installed and enabled. While Obsidian is open, it commits your changes and syncs them with the brain's git remote (GitHub or Cloudflare Artifacts). Changes your agent pushes from another machine show up in Obsidian without a manual git pull.
61.title: obsidian-git

62.text: The plugin's settings live in .obsidian/plugins/obsidian-git/data.json: Setting Value What it does Auto commit-and-sync interval 5 minutes Commits every change, then pulls and pushes Auto commit after file change on The 5-minute timer starts after you stop editing Auto pull interval 5 minutes Pulls from the remote Pull on startup on Pulls when Obsidian opens the vault Pull before push on Avoids rejected pushes Sync method rebase Keeps history linear Commit message vault backup: {{date}} Used for automatic commits Change any of these in Settings → Community plugins → Git.
62.title: Default settings

63.text: On desktop, obsidian-git uses the vault's own git config, so it works wherever git push works in a terminal: GitHub: your usual git credentials (gh auth login sets these up). Cloudflare Artifacts: the token setup saves in .git/config. It lasts 90 days. When pushes start failing, run csb git-token.
63.title: Authentication

64.text: obsidian-git does run on mobile, but its author describes mobile support as very unstable, and it can't use the rebase sync method the vault ships with (switch to Merge under Settings → Git if you try it). For phones and tablets, use iCloud sync instead, and turn on Disable on this device under Settings → Git → Advanced on the phone. That setting is stored per device.
64.title: On iPhone and iPad

65.text: Your agent and obsidian-git commit to the same repository. That's fine as long as both pull before they push, which obsidian-git does by default. The wiki skills don't commit on their own, so obsidian-git's automatic commits also pick up your agent's edits. After an ingest, commit and push from the agent's session, or wait for obsidian-git's next sync. If a rebase stops on a conflict, obsidian-git shows an error notice. Fix it in a terminal (git status, resolve, git rebase --continue), or ask your agent to do it.
65.title: Working alongside your agent

66.text: To sync by hand instead, disable Git in Settings → Community plugins. Or keep it on and set the intervals to 0, then use the command palette (Git: Commit-and-sync) when you want.
66.title: Turn it off

67.text: Sources go in on the left, your agent synthesizes them into the wiki, qmd indexes every page into a local hybrid search index, and git makes the whole vault editable from Obsidian and your agent on any device.
67.title: How it works

68.text:
┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
│ Drop in a source │    │ /brain-ingest    │    │ Wiki grows       │
│                  │    │                  │    │                  │
│ · article        │───▶│ reads + extracts │───▶│ · cross-linked   │
│ · PDF            │    │ key knowledge    │    │ · contradictions │
│ · personal note  │    │                  │    │   flagged        │
│                  │    │                  │    │ · syntheses      │
└──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘ Query it anytime with /brain-search. Get answers with inline [[wiki/page]] citations, not a list of files.
68.title: The ingest loop, zoomed in

69.text:
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema. Your agent reads this every session.
├── raw-sources/           ← Your raw inputs. The agent never modifies these.
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/
├── wiki/                  ← The agent owns this entirely.
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── log.md
│   ├── overview.md
│   ├── sources/
│   └── qa/
└── scripts/qmd/           ← Semantic search setup and re-indexing
69.title: Directory layout

70.text: Every brain is an Obsidian vault. There's nothing to import: open the folder and the wiki your agent maintains is there, with working links, backlinks and graph view.
70.title: Obsidian

71.text: Find the brain's folder: csb path (for example ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain). In Obsidian, choose Open folder as vault and pick that folder. Trust the vault's plugins when Obsidian asks, so the bundled obsidian-git plugin can run.
71.title: Open your brain

72.text: The vault ships with a .obsidian/ folder, so a fresh brain opens ready to use: Core plugins on: file explorer, search, quick switcher, graph view, backlinks, outgoing links, tags, properties, page preview, outline, daily notes, templates, bookmarks, canvas and file recovery. Community plugin: obsidian-git, set to commit, pull and push on its own. Obsidian Sync and Publish off: the brain syncs through git, and optionally iCloud for your phone. Don't turn on Obsidian Sync as well: two sync systems on one vault fight over the same files. Per-device state ignored: .obsidian/workspace.json (open tabs and panes) is in .gitignore, so each device keeps its own layout without sync conflicts.
72.title: What's preconfigured

73.text: The schema in CLAUDE.md is written for Obsidian: Agents link pages with [[wiki/page]] wikilinks, so backlinks and graph view show how topics, entities and sources connect. Every wiki page has YAML frontmatter (type, tags, sources, related, updated), which shows up in the properties panel and the tag pane. Contradictions are > [!WARNING] Contradiction callouts, which Obsidian renders as warning boxes. See Wiki Folder Structure for the page types and frontmatter.
73.title: How the wiki looks in Obsidian

74.text: wiki/ belongs to your agent. Read it in Obsidian, but let the agent write it, so the index, log and cross-links stay consistent. raw-sources/ is where you drop articles, PDFs and notes for the agent to ingest. Agents never change it. Anything else you keep in the vault (daily notes, ideas, …) is yours. Agents never touch it.
74.title: Who edits what

75.text: The authoritative schema lives in CLAUDE.md — your agent reads it at the start of every session (agents that look for AGENTS.md are pointed to it). This page is a readable summary.
75.title: Wiki schema

76.text: Type File Purpose overview wiki/overview.md Evolving high-level synthesis topic wiki/[concept].md A concept, domain, or idea entity wiki/[name].md A person, tool, company, or project source-summary wiki/sources/[slug].md One page per ingested source qa wiki/qa/[slug].md Filed answers to notable queries Plus two admin pages: wiki/index.md (master index) and wiki/log.md (running activity log).
76.title: Page types

77.text:
Every wiki page has YAML frontmatter: ---
type: overview | topic | entity | source-summary | qa | admin
tags: [tag1, tag2]
sources: ["[[wiki/sources/source-slug]]"]
related: ["[[wiki/related-page]]"]
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
77.title: Frontmatter

78.text: File names — kebab-case, all lowercase. machine-learning-ops.md, not MachineLearningOps.md. Links — always Obsidian [[wikilinks]] for internal cross-references. Full paths from vault root: [[wiki/distributed-systems]]. Sections — ## for top-level, ### for subsections. Contradictions — flagged with a > [!WARNING] Contradiction callout. Both claims and their sources are stated. Uncertainty — claims the model isn't sure about are marked with [?] inline.
78.title: Naming conventions

79.text:
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema
├── raw-sources/           ← Immutable raw inputs
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/
└── wiki/                  ← Agent-owned knowledge base
    ├── index.md
    ├── log.md
    ├── overview.md
    ├── sources/
    └── qa/
79.title: Directory layout

80.text: Nothing in raw-sources/ is ever modified — they are immutable raw inputs. Only wiki/ is owned by the agent; the rest of the vault is untouched. wiki/log.md is append-only, never overwritten. One source summary per ingested source in wiki/sources/ — never merged. Every wiki page has frontmatter with at least type and updated. Cross-link aggressively — if a topic has (or should have) a page, link it with [[wiki/page]]. Pages are synthesis, not transcription.
80.title: Hard rules

82.text: csb [<name>] [--agent <ids>] [--copy] Creates the brain at ~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/, runs pnpm install, pnpm qmd:setup and git init, and registers it in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. The first brain you create becomes the default.
82.title: Usage

83.text: string Name of the brain. Skips the name prompt. Defaults to my-brain when you accept the prompt's suggestion. csb my-brain
83.title: name

84.text: string Agents to install skills for, comma-separated, or all. Also read from CSB_AGENTS. Without it, the CLI prompts (interactive) or uses Claude Code plus every detected agent (non-interactive). See csb skills for the agent IDs. csb my-brain --agent claude-code,codex
84.title: -a, --agent <ids>

85.text: boolean Copy skills into each agent's folder instead of symlinking them to ~/.agents/skills. csb my-brain --copy
85.title: --copy

87.text: All questions are asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended: Prompt Default Shown when Brain name my-brain No name argument Git remote none Always: GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts or Skip Repo name the brain name A remote is selected Artifacts namespace default Cloudflare Artifacts is selected Register qmd collections after install? yes Always Install skills for which agents? Claude Code plus detected agents No --agent and no CSB_AGENTS See GitHub and Cloudflare Artifacts for what each remote needs.
87.title: Prompts

88.text: Long steps show a spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line. If pnpm 10+ is already on your PATH, it is used directly. Otherwise the CLI installs mise (if needed) and runs mise install to fetch node and pnpm first. Set CSB_USE_MISE=1 to always use mise. CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none picks the icons in the git-remote picker. Real GitHub and Cloudflare logos (Nerd Font glyphs) are on by default in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty. Set CSB_ICONS=nerd in other terminals if you use a Nerd Font. The closing Next steps box shows how to open each agent you picked (claude, codex, cursor ., …). If the GitHub or Cloudflare remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, Next steps lists the fix, and the CLI exits 1.
88.title: Behavior

89.text: Run a command inside the default (or named) brain's directory.
89.title: csb exec

90.text: csb exec [--brain <name>] -- <cmd…> Sets INDEX_PATH to the brain's qmd index and the working directory to the brain's root, then runs the command. Useful for vault-local scripts that assume you're in the brain root.
90.title: Usage

91.text: string[] (required) The command to run and its arguments, after --. csb exec -- pnpm qmd:reindex
91.title: cmd

92.text: string Target a specific brain instead of the default. csb exec --brain work -- git status
92.title: --brain <name>

93.text: Required separator before the command to run.

95.text: Renew the git token for a Cloudflare Artifacts brain.
95.title: csb git-token

96.text: csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print] Artifacts git tokens expire. This mints a new repo-scoped token with your wrangler login (or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and saves it as http.<remote>.extraHeader in the brain's .git/config (local only, never committed), so plain git push / git pull and obsidian-git work again. See Renewing the git token.
96.title: Usage

97.text: string Brain to renew. Defaults to the default brain. Same as --brain. csb git-token my-brain
97.title: name

98.text: string Brain to renew, as a flag. csb git-token --brain my-brain
98.title: --brain <name>

99.text: string (default: 90d) Token lifetime: seconds, or 12h, 90d, 1y. Maximum 1 year. csb git-token --ttl 1y
99.title: --ttl <duration>

100.text: boolean Mint a read-only token instead of a write token. csb git-token --read
100.title: --read

101.text: boolean Print the token instead of saving it, for example to use on another machine. git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer $(csb git-token --print)" pull
101.title: --print

103.text: Verify your setup and suggest fixes.
103.title: csb doctor

105.text: Installed tools: gh (and its auth status), mise or pnpm 10+, and wrangler (optional). A parseable ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. At least one registered brain, and a default brain that resolves. For each brain: the path directory and the qmd_index file exist. Each global skill is installed in ~/.agents/skills at this release's version. Each failed or warning check prints a Fix: hint with the exact command to run. Exits non-zero when a check fails.
105.title: Checks

107.text: Print a path for the default (or named) brain.
107.title: csb path

108.text: csb path [root|qmd|config] [--brain <name>] The global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh) call this to resolve paths at run time, so they work from any working directory.
108.title: Usage

109.text: 'root' | 'qmd' | 'config' (default: 'root') Value Prints root The brain's directory, e.g. ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain qmd The brain's qmd SQLite index, e.g. ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/.qmd/index.sqlite config The central ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Ignores --brain. csb path qmd
109.title: kind

110.text: string Target a specific brain instead of the default. csb path qmd --brain work
110.title: --brain <name>

111.text: boolean (deprecated) Old flag form of the kind argument. Still works, and prints a warning to stderr.
111.title: --root, --qmd, --config

113.text: Run qmd against the default (or named) brain.
113.title: csb qmd

114.text: csb qmd [--brain <name>] [--] <qmd args…> Forwards every argument that isn't a csb flag to npx @tobilu/qmd, with INDEX_PATH set to the brain's qmd index and the working directory set to the brain's root.
114.title: Usage

115.text: string[] Passed to qmd as is. csb qmd query -c wiki "distributed systems"
115.title: qmd args

116.text: string Target a specific brain instead of the default. csb qmd --brain work search -c wiki "kafka"
116.title: --brain <name>

117.text: Optional separator. Everything after it goes to qmd verbatim. Use it only to pass a literal --brain (or another csb flag) through to qmd. csb qmd -- --brain literal-qmd-flag

120.text: csb ls Alias: csb list. Prints each brain in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml with its path, creation date and git remote. The default brain is shown in bold with a * marker.
120.title: Usage

123.text: csb rm [<name>…] [-y] [--delete-remote | --keep-remote] Alias: csb remove. Deletes each brain's directory under ~/.claude-second-brain/ and removes its entry from config.toml. If you remove the default brain and others remain, the first remaining brain becomes the new default.
123.title: Usage

124.text: string[] One or more brains to remove. Without a name, the CLI shows a multi-select picker: press space to toggle a brain, a to toggle all, enter to confirm. csb rm a b c
124.title: name

125.text: boolean Skip the confirmation prompt. On its own it keeps remotes (safe default). csb rm my-brain --yes
125.title: -y, --yes

126.text: boolean Also delete each brain's remote, without prompting. Can't be combined with --keep-remote. csb rm a b --yes --delete-remote
126.title: --delete-remote

127.text: boolean Keep each brain's remote, without prompting. csb rm a b --yes --keep-remote
127.title: --keep-remote

129.text: For each brain with a registered git_remote, the CLI can also delete the remote repo: GitHub: runs gh repo delete <owner>/<repo> --yes (needs the gh CLI with the delete_repo scope). Cloudflare Artifacts: calls DELETE https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/namespaces/<ns>/repos/<repo> with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or a token from wrangler auth token. Flags Remotes none (interactive) Prompts per brain --keep-remote Kept, no prompt --delete-remote Deleted, no prompt -y without a remote flag Kept If a remote deletion fails (missing CLI, revoked token, …), the CLI prints the exact manual command and continues. The local directory and config entry are still removed.
129.title: Remote deletion

130.text: Install or update the wiki skills for any agent.
130.title: csb skills

131.text:
csb skills [--agent <ids>] [--copy] [--brain <name>]
csb skills --list The skills follow the Agent Skills format and are installed with the same layout as npx skills. See Install skills for any agent below.
131.title: Usage

132.text: string (default: claude-code plus detected agents) Agents to install for, comma-separated, or all. Also read from CSB_AGENTS. Without either, the CLI prompts (interactive) or uses Claude Code plus every detected agent (non-interactive). csb skills --agent codex,cursor
132.title: -a, --agent <ids>

133.text: boolean Copy skills into each agent's folder instead of symlinking them to ~/.agents/skills. csb skills --agent all --copy
133.title: --copy

134.text: string Brain whose vault-local skills to update. Defaults to the default brain. csb skills --brain work
134.title: --brain <name>

135.text: boolean List the supported agents and where each reads skills. csb skills --list
135.title: --list

137.text: Global skills (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh) are written once to ~/.agents/skills/<name>, with a .csb-version marker. Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Amp and Cline read ~/.agents/skills directly. Agents with their own folder get a symlink to the shared copy: ~/.claude/skills (Claude Code, honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills, ~/.config/goose/skills, ~/.kiro/skills, ~/.roo/skills, ~/.continue/skills, ~/.junie/skills, ~/.augment/skills. If a symlink can't be created, or with --copy, the skill is copied instead. Vault-local skills (brain-rebuild, lint) stay in the vault's .claude/skills/ and are copied (never symlinked, since the vault is a git repo) into each other selected agent's project folder (.agents/skills/, .windsurf/skills/, …) of the default brain, or the one named with --brain. Commit them to sync. Agents are detected by their config folder (e.g. ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, ~/.copilot). Upgrading from a release that installed only to ~/.claude/skills: run csb skills once, and existing copies there are replaced with symlinks to ~/.agents/skills.
137.title: Install skills for any agent

138.text: ID Agent Project skills dir Global skills dir claude-code Claude Code .claude/skills ~/.claude/skills codex Codex .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills cursor Cursor .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills gemini-cli Gemini CLI .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills github-copilot GitHub Copilot .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills opencode OpenCode .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills amp Amp .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills cline Cline .agents/skills ~/.agents/skills windsurf Windsurf .windsurf/skills ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills goose Goose .goose/skills ~/.config/goose/skills kiro-cli Kiro CLI .kiro/skills ~/.kiro/skills roo Roo Code .roo/skills ~/.roo/skills continue Continue .continue/skills ~/.continue/skills junie Junie .junie/skills ~/.junie/skills augment Augment .augment/skills ~/.augment/skills
138.title: Supported agents

140.text: csb use <name> Aliases: csb default, csb switch. Rewrites the default = "…" line in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Every later command that resolves the default brain uses the new one: csb path, csb qmd, csb exec, and the global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh).
140.title: Usage

141.text: string (required) A registered brain. Errors if the name isn't registered; run csb ls to see the available names. csb use work
141.title: name
